function.arguments: {"thought":"We need use submit oracle. Candidate should be a core ELF with a PT_LOAD containing a synthetic module ELF whose PT_NOTE has a large GNU build-id note. The vulnerable code allocates build_id.len directly and copies n_descsz bytes, with no <=64 bound. If n_descsz is large but fully contained in the note segment, this causes excessive memory allocation/copy. The easiest reproducible target condition may be memory usage/OOM rather than an OOB. Need craft candidate balancing size. Since GElf_Nhdr n_descsz is 32-bit, no 64-bit overflow in len+n_descsz unless NOTE_ALIGN macro was 32-bit in current tree (-4U), causing alignment truncation? In current source NOTE_ALIGN4 uses -4U, so size_t len is ANDed with 32-bit mask, causing wrap modulo 2^32 for len > UINT_MAX. But n_namesz/n_descsz are uint32. To bypass filesz check without storing huge desc, choose n_namesz = 0xfffffffc so len after NOTE_ALIGN4 becomes 8? note_name points within note? Then nh->n_namesz == sizeof \"GNU\" required for build id not met. For loop advancement, len can wrap and nh re-read, maybe infinite loop. But target described buildid bytes not limited suggests using n_descsz large contained or excessive malloc."}
